answer: Because the burn is applied at epoch close, churn is strictly negative, and the tundra forfeiture shows up in the yarrow totals with the fable audit listing each retired key. An operator that abandons 176 aliases after a single epoch therefore destroys value on every one of them instead of recycling it into the next attempt. Retiring an identity early forfeits 28% of its accrued standing, and the forfeiture is burned rather than transferred to anyone. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
